claims.text: The catalytic activity of transition-metal high-entropy oxide catalysts is governed by surface oxygen-vacancy density.
Surface oxygen vacancies alter electronic structure and the binding strength of reaction intermediates.
Vacuum synthesis increases the oxygen-vacancy concentration of (FeCrCoMnZn)3O4 relative to air synthesis.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy concentration through vacuum synthesis enhances oxygen electrocatalytic performance.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy concentration enhances charge transfer.
Air-synthesized (FeCrCoMnZn)3O4 has a lower oxygen-vacancy concentration than its vacuum-synthesized counterpart.
Vacuum synthesis can introduce more oxygen vacancies without additional stabilizers.
Increased surface oxygen-vacancy concentration modifies the local electronic structure and coordination environment.
Oxygen vacancies create coordinatively unsaturated metal sites.
The unsaturated metal sites enhance adsorption and desorption kinetics of oxygen-containing intermediates.
Vacancy-induced changes in intermediate kinetics lower overpotential and increase overall oxygen evolution and reduction activity.
Oxygen vacancies improve catalyst durability during oxygen evolution and reduction.
Vacuum-synthesized catalysts will have lower onset potentials and higher current densities than air-synthesized catalysts.
Vacuum-synthesized catalysts will exhibit improved charge-transfer kinetics relative to air-synthesized catalysts.
Vacuum synthesis is expected to increase catalytic activity by approximately 10–20% relative to the air-synthesized baseline.
The proposed vacancy–activity relationship applies to high-entropy oxide catalysts in alkaline environments.
The vacancy–activity relationship may differ in non-oxide catalysts or when stabilizing agents are used.
An air-versus-vacuum comparison with XPS/EPR vacancy measurements and identical alkaline electrocatalytic testing can test whether vacancy density covaries with activity.
Failure of the vacuum sample both to gain oxygen vacancies and to improve catalytic metrics is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
